states.name: focus-lg
states.pixelNote: Out of the pixel diff, measured rather than assumed. Figma's text node for "Link" is 35 CSS px wide and Chromium advances the same string, font and size to 34: the glyph ink is identical in both exports (33 CSS px, measured column by column), so Figma reserves about half a pixel of extra side bearing and rounds the box up. Every state reports that as PIXEL-SIZE-MISMATCH and shrugs it off, because their ink ends before the edge — but the focus ring hugs the box, so the reference paints that extra column solid #3379DB for the full height and the diff counts 136 of its 260 pixels there, 2.4% of the canvas on its own. The ring is pinned exactly by style parity instead (boxShadow, borderTopLeftRadius) and by the export's own geometry: 82x68 at scale 2 is the 35x28 label box with a 3px bleed on every side.

expect.note: Figma 57:465 carries the effect Focus Ring/Small, listed as 0px 0px 0px 3px rgba(51,121,219,1), 0px 0px 0px 1px rgba(255,255,255,1). Figma stacks those spreads: the render is a 1px white halo with the blue band ending 3px out, so in CSS the order reverses and the outer spread is the total 3px, not 1px + 3px. The underline stays 1px (57:467), as at rest. The ring has square corners: 57:465 carries no corner radius, and the exported node shows solid blue into the corner pixel — so the container radius is 0.
Figma 564:19598 paints the Strict label #121212 and 564:19599 the underline in the same ink; the type ramp is unchanged from Primary.

Figma 564:19476 paints the White label #FFFFFF and 564:19477 the underline in the same white. Out of the pixel diff on purpose: the Figma export is transparent around the glyphs and both images are flattened onto the page background, so white-on-white would compare two blank canvases and report a pass that means nothing. The colour is checked here instead.

The Underline options section (661:6990) shows the set twice, labelled "underline" and "underline-none". 661:7017 is the second: the same Primary/Large component with the boolean property off, so the underline frame is not drawn and the label keeps #0058D2.

states.name: target-pointer-lg
states.pixelNote: The Figma node is a documentation instance wearing a translucent #2F56FF overlay that marks the hit area, not something the component paints, so there is nothing to compare pixel for pixel. The height it annotates is pinned below.

expect.note: Figma's Target Sizes section (661:7040) says "the touch target should be increased to 32px" on pointer devices and draws it as a 2px halo around the 28px label box of 661:7043 — 28 + 2x2 = 32. The rendered gap above and below the label measures 2px, so the halo matches. Touch (40px, halo 6px, node in the second row of the same section) cannot be pinned here — the manifest has no way to emulate pointer: coarse — and was measured in Chromium under touch emulation instead.
